A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete versions of the same SPD paper. Their methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; v2 retains Appendices A–B and adds Appendix C.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLaMA2 and OPT accuracy, latency, and sensitivity experiments, plus MMLU results and a residual-placement ablation in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark figures and the appendix ablation table.

M1.justification: The block designs, sensitivity-ranking procedure, distillation objective, and head-grouping method remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. Appendix C explains the existing procedure and possible deployment combinations without revising SPD.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText2 calibration and perplexity evaluation, the same six zero-shot tasks, and MMLU. The data, pipeline, and hybrid parallelism examples added in Appendix C are conceptual scenarios, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding figures retain the same No SPD comparator and ZS, ZS+B2B, and ZS+B2B+HG variants. Table 1 retains the same residual-placement alternatives. Pipeline parallelism is discussed but not evaluated as a new baseline.

E3.justification: The model/GPU configurations, calibration samples, distillation budgets, and evaluation settings remain unchanged. Figure 7 now specifies time to first token for its existing latency plots; this discloses the timing target without documenting a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The sensitivity analysis, component comparisons, and Appendix B residual-placement ablation are retained unchanged. Appendix C adds explanatory discussion rather than new ablations, robustness tests, or measured supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results.

E6.justification: The plotted results and Table 1 values are unchanged. Section 5.3 retains the reported 19.7% speedup with 0.94% accuracy loss for LLaMA2-70B at 70% SPD under the same setting. Figure 7's caption clarification introduces no new measurements.

T1.justification: The block-output expressions, sensitivity definition, and objectives in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Appendix C supplies qualitative reasoning, without adding formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about SPD's block design, sensitivity-based strategies, and accuracy–latency trade-off. The headline LLaMA2-70B performance claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explains the rationale for suffix-based sensitivity measurement, discusses compatibility with data/pipeline/hybrid parallelism, and argues for SPD-enhanced tensor parallelism in compute-intensive prefill settings. These expand mechanism and applicability discussion without new comparative evidence.

D1.justification: Figure 7 newly identifies the latency endpoint as time to first token. Appendix C.2 adds illustrative GPU-replication and pipeline arrangements. These are additional reporting and deployment details; the documented training settings and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and Related Works section are unchanged, but Appendix C.3 adds positioning against pipeline parallelism through communication-overhead and compute-utilization arguments, particularly for prefill.

P1.justification: V2 adds a three-part Discussion appendix, acknowledgements, and correspondence/publication information, alongside small wording edits. The existing main-text organization and narrative are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 7 have revised captions, and the publication footer and appended discussion cause limited layout reflow. The existing diagrams, plots, algorithm display, and table structure remain, with no new visualizations.

improvement.justification: Identifying Figure 7's timing measure as time to first token resolves an ambiguity in v1, while Appendix C adds useful methodological rationale and deployment context. The improvement is limited to clarity and interpretation: experimental support is unchanged, and the new parallelism combinations and TP-versus-PP arguments receive no direct comparative validation.
